insights.headline: Gold and silver slip in MCX evening trade as a firm dollar and profit-booking stall Monday's rebound
insights.summary: MCX gold opened 0.7% lower at Rs 1,25,112 per 10 g in the evening session and silver fell 2.35% to Rs 1,50,591 per kg, giving back part of Monday's sharp rebound after a holiday-shut morning session. Spot gold held just above $3,630 an ounce and silver near $42.27 as the dollar index tested 104.50 and markets priced a 93.5% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Traders now await October US PCE inflation due Wednesday, the next test for the rebound ahead of the Fed's 9 December decision.
points: MCX gold opened 0.7% lower at Rs 1,25,112 per 10 g in the evening session; silver fell 2.35% to Rs 1,50,591 per kg.
Spot gold held just above $3,630 an ounce while silver slipped to about $42.27 as the dollar index tested 104.50.
MCX traded only the evening session for Guru Nanak Jayanti; NSE and BSE were shut for the day.
Natixis warns gold could fall to $3,340 by January as higher rates, a stronger dollar and slowing central-bank buying weigh.
Central banks bought 321 tonnes of gold in Q3 2026, the World Gold Council says, and global ETF holdings hit a record 4,275 tonnes.

brief.headline: Bullion slips in evening trade as dollar stays firm
brief.summary: MCX gold eased to Rs 1,25,112 per 10 g and silver to Rs 1,50,591 per kg as the dollar firmed; core PCE due Wednesday.

bullets.text: Profit-booking after Monday's rebound and a firm dollar near a 20-month high weighed on bullion, Moneycontrol and Reuters report.
MCX traded only the evening session for Guru Nanak Jayanti; the rupee could firm to 91.50 per dollar on equity inflows, Reuters reports.
Watch Wednesday: US core PCE at 19:00 IST, the next test for the rebound ahead of the Fed's 9 December decision.

trending.title: Rebound stalls in evening trade
trending.summary: Monday's sharp bounce faded on Tuesday as profit-booking and a firm dollar pushed MCX gold and silver lower in the evening session, with traders waiting on US PCE inflation due Wednesday.

trending.title: Silver under heavier pressure
trending.summary: Silver fell further than gold on Tuesday and is testing support near $40 after losing about 15% last week; MCX silver is down about Rs 1 lakh per kg in three months.

trending.title: Holiday-thin trading on MCX
trending.summary: Guru Nanak Jayanti shut the morning session and the equity markets, leaving only the MCX evening session to set the day's tone for bullion.

trending.title: Fed path decides the next move
trending.summary: Markets price a 93.5% chance of a December rate hike, so Wednesday's US core PCE and the Fed's 9 December decision are the next tests for the rebound.

items.title: Bullion tumbles again: Gold slips 0.7%, silver nearly 3% down; Three US triggers to watch
items.summary: MCX December gold futures opened 0.7% lower at Rs 1,25,112 per 10 g in the evening session and silver fell 2.35% to Rs 1,50,591 per kg, giving back part of Monday's sharp rebound. Spot gold held just above $3,630 an ounce while silver slipped to about $43, with traders awaiting US PCE inflation ahead of the Fed's December meeting.

items.title: Gold slips with spotlight on US inflation data
items.summary: Spot gold slipped 0.5% to $3,611.99 an ounce by 0827 GMT on Tuesday after rising nearly 3% in the previous session, as expectations of further US rate hikes and a dollar near a 20-month high weighed on prices. Silver fell 2.4% to $42.04. Traders now await Wednesday's US PCE inflation data, the last key reading before the Fed's final meeting of 2026.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: Strong Dollar Puts $40 Support at Risk
items.summary: Silver slipped 2.09% to $42.27 an ounce on Tuesday as Monday's rebound lost momentum and the dollar index tested resistance at 104.50. Markets price a 93.5% chance of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, FXEmpire reports, ahead of October PCE inflation due Wednesday. The article puts key support at $39–$40, warning a break below it could open a drop toward $35–$37.

items.title: Gold, silver prices see sharp rebounds as AI shares rally, renewed Fed uncertainty
items.summary: Spot gold traded near $3,635.10 an ounce late Monday, up 2.75%, and silver around $43.02, up about 4.6%, as bargain hunting and improving risk sentiment lifted metals after last week's selloff, Kitco reports. Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, steadying equities, though Fed tightening concerns, high Treasury yields and geopolitical uncertainty still challenge the recovery.

items.title: Silver price crash: Rates today in India down ₹1 lakh in 3 months! Recovery or more fall ahead for MCX silver futures?
items.summary: Silver in India is down about ₹1 lakh per kg in three months from its August high of around ₹2.5 lakh, with MCX silver closing Monday at ₹1,54,205 per kg after a ₹6,392 rebound. Market experts attribute the slide to elevated US bond yields, a strong dollar, talk of a US Fed rate hike and the rupee's rise from around 98 to 92.50 per dollar; they put crucial support at ₹1,40,000 per kg.

items.title: Gold edges up on bargain buying after selloff; US inflation data awaited
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.4% to $3,645.29 an ounce in early Asian trade, extending Monday's rebound from a 14-month low, while silver climbed 1.2% to $43.55. Markets now await Wednesday's US PCE inflation data, with traders pricing a 95% chance of a December Fed rate rise.

items.title: Gold, Silver Price Outlook 2027: Is A Big Recovery Coming?
items.summary: Gold is down about 35% from its 12-month peak and silver 60–65% from its high, ETV Bharat reports, with MCX gold about 30% below its January peak of Rs 1,80,779 per 10 g. Ajay Kedia of Kedia Advisory expects gold could reach $5,000 an ounce within a year. The article cites higher US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar, and notes central banks bought 321 tonnes of gold in Q3 2026.

items.title: Gold Rebounds as Huang's Return to Nvidia Revives Risk Appetite
items.summary: Gold extended its rebound after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, rising as much as 4.3% to $3,690 an ounce after a near-9% slide last week. Bloomberg reports the selling was concentrated in futures, while ETF holdings stayed steady, according to UBS, and retail dip-buying emerged in Shenzhen jewellery markets. Fed officials still back higher rates to fight sticky inflation.

items.title: Gold Climbs To Rs 1.28 Lakh Per 10 Grams, Silver Recovers
items.summary: Retail gold climbed to nearly Rs 1.28 lakh per 10 g on Tuesday — 24-carat gold around Rs 1,27,800, up Rs 1,240 — snapping a 10-session losing streak in the national capital, while retail silver hovered near Rs 1.55 lakh per kg. MCX December gold futures settled 3.8% higher at Rs 1,28,912 per 10 g on Monday, and spot gold stood near $3,645 an ounce.

MCX gold futures rose 2.2% and silver 2.11% on Monday after last week's slide — gold fell 11% and silver 16.2% on the week — as short covering and bargain buying met a softer dollar and fading bets on Fed hikes. Spot gold traded near $3,609, up 2%, and silver just above $42. Analysts quoted remain cautious, saying the rebound must hold above resistance to confirm a turn.
items.title: Gold and silver rebound over 2% after steep weekly losses: Can the recovery sustain?

items.summary: MCX December gold futures rose Rs 2,899, or 2.38%, to Rs 1,24,677 per 10 grams as speculators built fresh positions on firm spot demand, PTI reported; silver futures gained 2.45% to Rs 1,51,435 per kg. In New York, gold futures rose 2.14% to $3,614.25 an ounce and silver futures 2.91%.
items.title: Gold futures rise to Rs 1.24 lakh per 10 grams, silver crosses Rs 1.51 lakh per kg
Domestic stock markets closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti; MCX to resume trading in evening session
items.summary: MCX will stay shut for its morning session on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti, with gold and silver futures trading resuming in the evening session from 5 pm; NSE and BSE are closed for the day and reopen on Wednesday.

items.title: Silver Recovery Watch: Identifying the Next Major Market Turning Point
items.summary: Silver futures steadied near $42.56 after correcting from a recent high near $47.92 to a low of $40.62, the analysis says, with $42.90 the immediate level to reclaim and $43.57 the weekly benchmark for buyers to regain control; holding above $41.68 keeps the recovery intact, while a break below the $40.62 low would point to more weakness.

items.title: Gold's recovery may be short-lived as Natixis warns of drop to $3,340
items.summary: Natixis precious metals analyst Bernard Dahdah warns gold's rebound above $3,600 may not hold, seeing a drop to $3,340 an ounce by January as higher rates, a stronger dollar and weaker investment demand weigh on the metal, Kitco reports. Natixis also sees signs that central-bank gold buying, a key support in recent years, is starting to slow.

items.title: Gold, Copper, Zinc, Aluminium: Morgan Stanley's outlook on key metals
items.summary: Morgan Stanley says gold's long-term drivers remain intact: physical demand is holding up, China's central bank added 26 tonnes in October, and ETF selling has been modest despite falling prices. It says gold could move higher if oil falls further or the market concludes the Fed has finished hiking, though short-term volatility may stay high.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2021-22 Series I premature redemption price at ₹12,612
items.summary: The RBI has fixed the premature redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2021-22 Series I at ₹12,612 per unit for the November 25 redemption, based on the average IBJA 999-purity gold close over November 19, 20 and 23. Holders who applied in the window that closed November 16 can exit at that price, a gain of up to 167% over the ₹4,727 online issue price.

items.title: Indian rupee could rise to 91.50/$ on equity inflows, HDFC Bank's treasury head says
items.summary: The rupee could strengthen to 91.50 per dollar if strong equity inflows continue, HDFC Bank treasury head Arup Rakshit said, seeing it in a 91.50-93.50 range near term. The currency closed Friday at 92.67, up nearly 2.5% in November on record $12 billion of foreign equity inflows, and Rakshit expects the RBI to raise rates in December, with a 25-basis-point hike more or less given.

items.title: Salem Anklet manufacturers see a silver lining as metal price dips Rs 2L/ kg in 10 months
items.summary: Salem's silver anklet makers say orders have recovered to nearly half of normal levels after more than a year of sluggish business, as silver fell to about Rs 175 a gram in the city from Rs 195 a week ago, the article reports. Workshops that ran about two days a week now work nearly six days a week ahead of Pongal.
